purpose: Insulin aspart is used to help control blood sugar levels in people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. It works specifically around mealtimes to prevent your blood sugar from rising too high after you eat. Keeping your blood sugar in a healthy range helps prevent serious complications like nerve damage, kidney problems, and vision loss.
how_it_works: Think of insulin as a key that unlocks the doors of your body's cells so sugar (glucose) from your food can get inside and be used for energy. Insulin aspart is a man-made insulin that works very similarly to the natural insulin your body makes, but it acts faster. It starts working within about 15 minutes, peaks in about 1 hour, and lasts for 2 to 4 hours, making it perfect for controlling the blood sugar spike that happens after meals.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can make you feel shaky, sweaty, dizzy, confused, or hungry — always carry a fast-acting sugar like glucose tablets or juice just in case. You may also notice redness, swelling, or a small lump at the injection site, but this usually goes away. Weight gain is also possible over time.
warnings: Never skip a meal after taking this insulin, as it can cause dangerously low blood sugar. Do not mix it up with long-acting insulin unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can make low blood sugar more likely and harder to notice. Tell your doctor right away if you are sick, as illness can change how much insulin you need. Do not share your insulin pen or needles with anyone else, even family members.
typical_dosing: This insulin is usually taken just before a meal — ideally within 5 to 10 minutes before you start eating (Fiasp can also be taken at the start of or within 20 minutes after beginning a meal). Your dose is personalized by your doctor based on your blood sugar levels, what you eat, and your overall health. Never change your dose on your own without checking with your doctor or diabetes care team first.
